title: Transportation Authority contractors paid for the sales-tax campaign
question: Did firms holding Transportation Authority contracts fund the 2022 campaign for the sales tax the Authority spends?
finding: Yes. Organisations gave $1.6 million to the Yes on L committee (Better Roads and Transit) in 2022-23; 8 of them are firms in the Authority's award memos on disk, $132,500 together: AECOM $35,000; Arup $25,000; HNTB Corporation $25,000; WSP USA Inc. $20,000; WMH Corporation $10,000; TY Lin International $10,000; DeSilva Gates Construction $5,000. WMH Corporation's $10,000 came on 3 June 2022, the month after the Board gave it the $2.7 million Hillcrest design contract, and it filed the City's contractor-contribution form for it; its three Authority contracts have since been amended upward.
how: Campaign transactions to committees named Better Roads and Transit, excluding individuals, counted once per transaction id; firm names matched to the awardees in the memos screen; the Hillcrest award date is from the April 2024 memo (Resolution 22-52, May 2022).
limits: Giving to a ballot-measure committee is permitted for contractors and is not a gift to any official; engineering firms routinely back transportation funding measures, which fund their whole industry. Firm names are matched on the organisation name only, and affiliates (such as a firm's political action committee) are counted with the firm.
